sn11.13:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesali in the Great Wood in the Hall with the Peaked Roof.
sn11.13:1.3: Then Mahāli the Licchavi approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and said to him:
sn11.13:2.1: “Venerable sir, has the Blessed One seen Sakka, lord of the devas?”
sn11.13:4.1: “Surely, venerable sir, that must have been one who looked like Sakka, lord of the devas; for Sakka, lord of the devas,
sn11.13:5.1: “I know Sakka, Mahāli, and I know the qualities that make for Sakka, by the undertaking of which Sakka achieved the status of Sakka. ”
sn11.13:6.1: “Mahāli, in the past, when Sakka, lord of the devas, was a human being, he was a brahmin youth named Magha; therefore he is called Maghavā.
sn11.13:7.1: Mahāli, in the past, when Sakka, lord of the devas, was a human being, he gave gifts in city after city; therefore he is called Purindada, the Urban Giver.
sn11.13:8.1: Mahāli, in the past, when Sakka, lord of the devas, was a human being, he gave gifts considerately; therefore he is called Sakka.
sn11.13:9.1: Mahāli, in the past, when Sakka, lord of the devas, was a human being, he gave a rest house; therefore he is called Vāsava.
sn11.13:10.1: Mahāli, Sakka, lord of the devas, thinks of a thousand matters in a moment; therefore he is called Sahassakkha, Thousand-eyed.
sn11.13:11.1: Mahāli, Sakka's wife is the asura maiden named Sujā; therefore he is called Sujampati, Sujā's husband.
sn11.13:12.1: Mahāli, Sakka, lord of the devas, exercises supreme sovereignty and rulership over the Tavatimsa devas; therefore he is called lord of the devas.
sn11.13:13.1: Mahāli, in the past, when Sakka, lord of the devas, was a human being, he adopted and undertook seven vows by the undertaking of which he achieved the status of Sakka.
sn11.13:13.3: ‘As long as I live may I support my parents.’
sn11.13:13.4: ‘As long as I live may I respect the family elders.’
sn11.13:13.5: ‘As long as I live may I speak gently.’
sn11.13:13.6: ‘As long as I live may I not speak divisively.’
sn11.13:13.7: ‘As long as I live may I dwell at home with a mind devoid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, delighting in relinquishment, devoted to charity, delighting in giving and sharing.’
sn11.13:13.8: ‘As long as I live may I speak the truth.’
sn11.13:13.9: ‘As long as I live may I be free from anger, and if anger should arise in me may I dispel it quickly.’
sn11.13:13.10: In the past, Mahāli, when Sakka, lord of the devas, was a human being, he adopted and undertook these seven vows by the undertaking of which he achieved the status of Sakka.
sn11.13:14.1: When a person supports his parents,
sn11.13:14.3: When his speech is gentle and courteous,
sn11.13:14.4: And he refrains from divisive words;
sn11.13:15.1: When he strives to remove meanness,
